$comment: Canonical wording for the electrical template — ADR-014 prerequisite B.
Template extraction is classification, not copying. Most customer-facing
text is safe universal copy and extracts automatically. This file holds the
text that is NOT: copy carrying a price, naming a contractor, stating a
company policy, or ambiguous enough that a machine should not decide.
The extractor FAILS when it meets such text and finds no entry here. It
never silently strips, generalises, or guesses — a label built around a
number has no mechanical rewrite, and inventing one would put words in a
`reason` is required and is the record of WHY a human had to decide.
`keys` remaps an Elite service slug to its canonical TEMPLATE key. It does
NOT rename anything of Elite's: their slug is a live URL and an operational
identifier, and there is no reason to break it to make the template clean.
Provenance records where the canonical service came from.

dedicated-120v-circuit-outlet/dedicated_.helpText: Depending on the wiring path available, this may require small access openings in finished surfaces near your electrical panel and at the new outlet, so the cable can enter the wall.
dedicated-120v-circuit-outlet/dedicated_.reason: Elite's paragraph combined two different things. That a run through finished space may need an access opening is a physical fact of the work and is kept, in neutral wording. That patching, spackling, sanding, painting, wallpaper and trim are excluded unless put in writing is a scope promise — the contractor's terms, not the trade's — and moves to the contractor's own disclaimer (ADR-009). Discarding the universal fact along with the policy would have lost real trade knowledge.

dedicated-120v-circuit-outlet/dedicated_.reason: Elite's label named the contractor. Naming them is not universal copy, and a mechanical substitution to 'we' reads oddly in a first-person answer the homeowner is choosing. Same sentence as new-120v-outlet/outlet_finish_ack/review_first, which was authored first.

exterior-gfci-other-routing/ext_gfci_fin.helpText:
With no attic, basement or drop ceiling to work through, the wiring for this outlet has to be fished through finished walls.

Your electrician will likely need to make one or more openings in the drywall or plaster to get the cable across. We keep them small and put them where they're least visible, but on a finished wall they usually can't be avoided entirely.

That's why we asked about attic and basement access — an open route usually means no openings at all and less time on site.
exterior-gfci-other-routing/ext_gfci_fin.reason: Elite's paragraph combined a physical fact with a scope promise. That fishing a cable through finished walls or ceilings requires access openings — and that an open route above or below usually avoids them — is true of the work whoever performs it, so it is kept in full. The paragraph excluding patching, sanding, painting, wallpaper and trim 'unless we've put it in writing' is the contractor's terms, not the trade's, and moves to their own disclaimer (ADR-009). Discarding the universal fact along with the policy would have thrown away real trade knowledge.

replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/(service).reason: Elite's name was 'Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan — We Supply the Fan'. Neutralizing the title does NOT delete the question — see bathroom_fan.supply_arrangement in electrical.policies.json, which keeps it as an unresolved contractor decision.
